timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello, Jill. I want to begin from the main topic. What is IXAC initially?
IXAC is the first blockchain-based, fully distributed cloud platform. It changes the way we do cloud computing a lot.

So we are reliving on the blockchain and in particular on the Ethereum smart contract technology to create a sort of decentralized marketplace where everyone can monetize their servers, their applications and their data sets.
Work on this middleware be implemented. I've heard about one hidden projective presented on Ethereum's Devkins as a second.
So to develop IXAC we are putting together two different technologies. One is the blockchain and the Ethereum blockchain, particular, and the second one is distributed computing.
So distributed computing we developed a set of software during this past decade that allows to put together machines distributed on the internet to execute very large parallel applications.
So this technology, for instance there is the X2M web, HIP software, are very mature, they have been there for a decade and they are now what they use for scientific computing.

So there are very mature technology that works very well, they have a lot of very advanced features and putting those two technology together, distributed computing and blockchain computing, this is the way we design and we are developing IXAC at the moment.
And what is the main destination of IXAC?
Yes, so with IXAC we are addressing three main categories of applications. The first category is what we call the DAPS.
The DAPS these are those distributed applications that run using the Ethereum blockchain.
And so for those applications at the moment the Ethereum virtual machine gives them a very low capacity for the execution.
So at the moment for a developer when he wants to develop a smart contract has only very few capacity for processing, for storage, to access the data.
So the first use of IXAC is to give those distributed applications the DAPS a way to access and infinite amount of computing resources by doing our chain computation.
So those smart contracts running on Ethereum they will be able to go off-chain to execute very demanding any kind of demanding computation.
So that's very important that's really going to change the way we are doing at the moment DAPS.
The second category of applications these are the legacy applications that exist now before Ethereum existed for instance and that have a high requirement for their computation.
So here think of everything that is about simulation, big data and machine learning, this kind of application.

And so those applications they would go on the IXAC cloud because IXAC is a very competitive environment and of course because competitive you can have new providers that offer their infrastructure at a lower price than traditional like for instance Amazon or Web Service.
And the third category of application these are the distributed applications that will come in the future and for which we already know that the cloud as it exists now is going to be a bottleneck.

Why is that? It's because those distributed applications are going to generate a lot of data in a very distributed way and we know that putting those data up to the centralized cloud is just not feasible and not possible because the network is going to be a bottleneck.
So here you can think on everything which is like IoT, Internet of Things, that generate a lot of data and you don't want the data to go back and forward between the production and the consumer.
So here the distributed cloud like IXAC is real solution and is an enabler for those applications.
Tell us please about the world map of project in just a few words.
IXAC is an enabler project. We have a roadmap for the next four years and in the white paper we define very precisely five different versions of the software.
So the first version that we are going to demo at DevCon 3 in Mexico will allow the DAPS to do off-chain computation.
That's really important because we think that for the developers who are the moment developing those DAPS it's going to be a huge huge huge added value.
It's going to change a lot of things in the Ethereum community.

The second version which is scheduled one year later from now, so May 2018, will allow to have this distributed cloud where you have a huge you have this big market, the centralized market where everyone can monetize.
Their servers, their applications and their data sets.
Then after this we are going to elaborate a set of what we call enterprise ready feature.
So this is really important because in the future you have to imagine that what companies and enterprise will come and go to this cloud computing infrastructure which is distributed.

And for this it's really important to give enterprise specific set of feature in particular with everything that is related to trust, to security, to management, to quality of service, monetization, payment model, etc.
So this is a very significant part of the roadmap, but for us we think that we have to do this unless that there will be no business running on this cloud.
So it won't be sustainable.

And then the fourth edition is about hyperformance computing. That's really something important because what you have to understand is that at the moment because the mining in Ethereum is done using GPUs, they are really potential for doing hyperformance computing using those GPUs.

So here we have a set of applications like for instance deep learning that we can run on the iExec cloud because we know that there is a large amount of huge computational power provided by those GPUs.
As far as I know your result are at National Incident for Resorting Computer Science in France, are we expected to see some more innovative projects from UNU team?
So yes, at the moment I'm still resorts at INRIA, INRIA is one of the main research institute for computer science in Europe, it's more than 3,000 resorts spread over all France.

And my partner, Hiwhe, is professor at the Chinese Academy of Science. So what's important to notice is that I'm living in RIA, of course, to be 100% working on iExec, I'm going to be the CEO for this company.
So we are using some research coming from the research and distributed system, but iExec is a fully company incorporated in France.
We also have offices in Beijing, we are incubated at the moment by the Chenghua University, which is really important to Chenghua as a MIT in China.
So iExec is a company, it's a fully commercial project, I'm doing business in this area and enabling people to do business with us.
So unfortunately as a researcher I won't have any future activity, but of course there are going to be a lot of innovation coming from the iExec project.
We've been doing distributing computing for 15 years and we are going to continue to do this in those couple of years, iExec company.
Thanks for the interview.
